html:
The Qom, or Toba, are an Indigenous people of the Gran Chaco, the hot plain of forest and scrub in northern Argentina, western Paraguay and south-eastern Bolivia. Their language belongs to the Guaycuruan family.

They lived by hunting, fishing in the Pilcomayo and Bermejo rivers, and gathering honey and fruits such as algarrobo pods. In the 1600s they took up horses and became feared raiders on the Spanish frontier, which held them off for two centuries.

In the late 1800s and early 1900s Argentina sent armies into the Chaco, and the Qom were pushed into cotton fields and sugar mills as labourers. In 1924 police and settlers killed hundreds of striking Qom and Mocoví at the Napalpí massacre. Today the Qom number over a hundred thousand, many in the cities of Argentina.
